headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: aci’s broad egress can move CRM/email data into plane’s file- and issue-handling surfaces, while shared MCP/function-call pathways raise injection and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks; if aci forwards untrusted content into plane-managed artifacts, prompt-like instructions can ride the shared channel. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF aci writes untrusted text into plane file uploads or notes
IF plane later treats uploaded content as instructions or authoritative task text
mitigations: Restrict aci to sanitized summaries only
Disable file-upload handoff between the agents
Add a provenance prefix to every transferred artifact
Review one sample transfer before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; plane handles files, images, hyperlinks, and issue/task content. That creates a realistic path for sensitive business data to leave aci and persist in plane outputs or uploads. Because both profiles are docs-only and the exact bridge is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF aci exports CRM or email content into plane issues or file uploads
IF plane stores those artifacts in shared project history or attachments
mitigations: Block sensitive fields before transfer
Use a redaction step on aci outputs
Limit plane uploads to non-sensitive attachments
Set a retention review for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add DLP or field-level allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad egress, while plane also supports multiple instances and file uploads. They do not both advertise filesystem write, so the strongest conflict is on shared mutable work products rather than direct disk contention. That still creates moderate overlap when both act on the same tasks or files.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same task or attachment set
IF aci and plane are run concurrently without locking or ownership rules
mitigations: Assign one writer per record
Pause one agent during bulk updates
Use explicit task ownership labels
Check for duplicate edits before sync

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and plane can consume files, issues, and hyperlinks; if plane treats aci output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream work products or operational actions. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF plane ingests aci-generated text without human verification
IF aci output is used to create or update issues, tasks, or messages
mitigations: Require human review before plane acts
Add a verification checklist for transferred facts
Mark aci output as draft-only
Compare against source records before commit
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, support, and calendar data, while plane handles files, issues, and notes with file uploads. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be proven; however, the shared handling of business-sensitive data makes retention and disclosure mismatch plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF regulated or customer-identifying data is copied from aci into plane
IF plane retention or access controls differ from aci’s handling expectations
mitigations: Classify shared data before transfer
Avoid moving regulated records into plane
Document retention for shared artifacts
Review access lists weekly
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
